about: This classic Lord of the Rings macro shows Sean Bean as Boromir at the Council of Elrond, mid-sentence, holding one hand up with his thumb and fingers curled into a loose circle as he lectures the room. His tone is grave and slightly condescending, the voice of a man explaining why a plan is far harder than everyone thinks. As a meme, the sentence is turned into a fill-in-the-blank: one does not simply do some everyday thing, implying it is a quest with hidden dangers. The humor comes from applying that epic warning to tasks like eating one chip or closing Vim.
origin: Boromir says the line in Peter Jackson's 2001 film The Fellowship of the Ring, the first Lord of the Rings movie, during the council that decides what to do with the One Ring. The hand gesture from that moment became one of the most recognizable image macros of the early 2010s.
usage:
The top box almost always reads "one does not simply" and the bottom box names the task that turns out to be impossible. That fixed opener is part of the recognition, so change only the second line.

Pick something that sounds easy but famously isn't: watching one episode, leaving a store with only what you came for, fixing one small bug, getting a straight answer from customer support. The more mundane the task, the funnier Boromir's solemn warning becomes.
ideas: walk past a dog without petting it
fix the bug on a friday
leave ikea in under two hours
aka: One Does Not Simply Walk into Mordor
